cur:catacombs-marcus-claudianus-sarcopha.summary: A long frieze shows the youthful Christ performing miracles – at Cana, of the loaves, healing the blind, raising Lazarus – and foretelling Peter's denial, while the lid holds one of the earliest Nativity scenes, with the Child watched by the ox, the ass and a shepherd. Old and New Testament scenes are interwoven, presenting Christ as a teacher-philosopher with wonder-working power.
facts: It was found in 1884 in Via della Lungara, near San Giacomo in Settimiana; the lid inscription names Lucius Valerius Claudius Maximus Claudianus, who died aged about 43.
Italian Wikipedia notes that it, with the Stilicho sarcophagus in Milan, preserves two of the earliest Nativity scenes, in which the Child appears without Mary and Joseph.

cur:objects-coin-michael-iii-sole-reign-.summary: The obverse bears the bust of Christ Pantokrator with a cross behind his head, surrounded by the legend IhSUS XRISTOS, 'Jesus Christ'. On the reverse Michael III appears alone, crowned and holding a labarum. After his mother's removal from power the emperor kept Christ's image in the place of honour on the coinage.
facts: After the post-iconoclast revival, the bust of Christ on the obverse with the emperor on the reverse became the standard design of Byzantine gold coinage (Wikipedia, Byzantine coinage).
